title: Benefit from public unlabeled data: A Frangi filtering-based pretraining network for 3D cerebrovascular segmentation
mechanism: Multi-task pretraining of the whole segmentation network on unlabeled data, with Frangi-filter-derived thin-structure maps as targets.
adaptation: Pretrain the full U-Net++ (decoder included) on the 11.9k pool, then the 159k, to regress multi-scale dark-ridge maps and the FFT periodic residual. Fine-tune with PF so the pretrained layers survive.
min_experiment: Arm: ridge-target pretraining 40k steps, then PF fine-tune, 5 seeds. Baseline: PF from ImageNet. Metric: crack IoU (CV), E1 relF1@2. Kill: < +0.012 crack IoU and < +0.02 on E1.
evidence: R: 1,510 unlabeled TOF-MRA plus 113 labelled subjects across 4 datasets; about +3% over SOTA semi- and self-supervised methods.
prior_overlap: MIM and DDeP pool pretraining were n.d.; section 5 explicitly leaves dense or thin-structure-aware objectives open.

alt_notes.adaptation: Dark-ridge filter (Frangi on inverted EL, sigma 1 to 2 px, plus black top-hat) on the de-duplicated pool; pretrain full U-Net++ R34 to regress the ridge map plus reconstruct the image; suppress busbar/finger ridges using house structural-class predictions; then house PF fine-tune.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Ridge-target pretraining on 11.9k (~20 GPU-h) then PF vs house PF and vs our MIM checkpoint; out-of-fold relF1@2 and E1 crack recall, 2 seeds; kill if relF1@2 < +0.005 and E1 recall < +0.02.
